stories.title: Everglades Foundation Nearly Doubling Footprint in South Florida
stories.excerpt: The Everglades Foundation is relocating to Dadeland, Fla., and nearly doubling its office footprint. The environmental nonprofit inked a 14,531-square-foot office lease at Two Datran Center in the Miami suburb. The tenant, which is scheduled to move next November, will occupy portions of the 14th and 15th floors inside the 20-story building. IP Capital Partners’ Two Datran Center spans 540,778 square feet at 9130 South Dadeland Boulevard, adjacent to Metrorail’s Dadeland South station, between Dixie Highway and Palmetto Expressway. The Everglades Foundation, which works to protect the national park, is currently based in a 8,533-square-foot office six miles south inside the Palmetto Bay Village Center at 18001 Old Cutler Road, according to a representative for JLL, whose Tyler de la Peña represented the tenant in the recent transaction. “With its central location, direct Metrorail access and on-site amenities, the new office will enhance the employee experience while creating more opportunities to collaborate with partners,” Coreen Rodgers, Everglades Foundation’s chief finance and operations officer, said in a statement. The complex is part of the two-building Datran Center complex, which totals 817,803 square feet and was completed in the 1980s. IP Capital Partners has owned the asset since 2016, and Cushman & Wakefield’s Jeannette Mendoza and Andrew Trench represented the Boca Raton-based investor in the transaction with the Everglades Foundation. The brokers did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Everglades Foundation leases 14,531 SF at Two Datran Center, Dadeland, FL; relocates from Palmetto Bay.
New office nearly doubles footprint; situated adjacent to Metrorail Dadeland South station.
Tenant migration signals office demand in transit-oriented Miami suburban nodes.
stories.summary: The Everglades Foundation is relocating its Miami-area headquarters to Two Datran Center in Dadeland, increasing its office footprint from 8,533 SF to 14,531 SF across the 14th and 15th floors. The move, closing in November, positions the nonprofit six miles north from its current Palmetto Bay location, leveraging the building's direct Metrorail access and central location. The transaction underscores continued office demand in the Miami suburbs, particularly in transit-connected nodes.
stories.impact: Reflects flight from car-dependent suburbs to transit-oriented infill in South Florida; signals potential headwind for multifamily in isolated Palmetto Bay, tailwind for mixed-use around Dadeland Metrorail. Developers should monitor whether this trend of corporate relocations to transit hubs replicates across Miami submarkets, strengthening rent growth near rail corridors.

stories.title: WestCap’s Kevin Marcus Takes Over as CEO of Green Street
stories.excerpt: Jeff Stuek is moving upward at commercial real estate intelligence platform Green Street as Kevin Marcus joins the firm as CEO. Marcus has been appointed to the role of CEO in Green Street’s New York City office as Stuek ascends to executive chair and a seat on the board of directors, in a move the firm anticipates will facilitate company growth, according to the firm. Stuek was CEO for seven years, during which time he built Green Street’s private markets and assets division, a news service and an infrastructure arm. He also explored new geographical markets and sectors for the company. “Leading Green Street for the past seven years has been a true privilege,” Stuek said in a statement. “Together with our talented team, we have expanded our business and brand while maintaining the high standards our clients depend on.” Marcus, meanwhile, previously worked as a partner and co-chief operating officer at global operating equity firm WestCap for six years ending earlier this month. He was also president and chief operating officer of Ipreo Private Capital Markets from 2006 to 2019, according to his LinkedIn page. “Green Street has achieved remarkable growth and global expansion, strengthening a trusted brand and building an exceptional team,” Marcus said in a statement. “Real assets represent one of the world’s largest asset classes, and demand for independent, high-quality data and insight has never been greater. We will continue to invest in our people and our platform and deepen integrations into our clients’ workflows, in order to deliver even more value to our clients.” Green Street provides a large array of services from asset class research, news content, data, analytics and advisory services. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Kevin Marcus appointed CEO of Green Street; held COO role at WestCap for 6 years.
Jeff Stuek promoted to executive chair after 7-year tenure building private markets division.
Leadership transition signals growth orientation at CRE intelligence platform.
stories.summary: Green Street, a commercial real estate intelligence platform, appointed Kevin Marcus as CEO, while founder/CEO Jeff Stuek ascends to executive chair. Marcus joins from WestCap, where he was partner and co-COO for six years, bringing private markets expertise. The transition is intended to facilitate company growth and expansion into new geographies and sectors.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, Green Street's expansion into private markets and new sectors could increase capital scrutiny and benchmarking rigor on apartment valuations and underwriting; watch for stricter cap rate and NOI expectations as the platform gains scale in real estate analytics.

stories.title: ViaWest Group and Walton Street Capital Buy Medical Office Campus in Gilbert, Arizona
stories.excerpt: A venture between ViaWest Group and Walton Street Capital has purchased Mercy Medical Campus, a two-building, 105,715-square-foot medical office portfolio in Gilbert, Arizona, in an off-market deal. The purchase includes Mercy Medical Commons I and II, situated on 11 acres at 3645 S. Rome Street and 3591 S. Mercy Road, across from the 400-bed Mercy Gilbert Medical Center. Constructed in 2010, Mercy Medical Commons I is a two-story building containing 47,017 square feet of space. Mercy Medical Commons II, built in 2020, is a three-story, 58,698-square-foot structure. The campus was designed by Ware Malcomb and built by Balfour Beatty. It is fully leased to nine healthcare industry tenants, including The CORE Institute, Arizona Center for Cancer Care, Scottsdale Medical Imaging (SMIL), Arizona Diagnostic Radiology (RadNet) and Arizona Center for Cancer Care (AZCCC). The Gilbert submarket has experienced significant growth in recent years, justifying an increasing need for healthcare services. The Mercy Medical Commons I and II campus is well-located to support the expanding medical needs of the Southeast Valley. bullets: ViaWest Group and Walton Street Capital acquire Mercy Medical Campus, Gilbert, AZ; 105,715 SF, two buildings.
Campus fully leased to 9 healthcare tenants; built 2010–2020; sits adjacent to 400-bed Mercy Gilbert Medical Center.
Gilbert submarket experiencing significant growth; acquisition reflects healthcare real estate demand in Southeast Valley.
stories.summary: A joint venture between ViaWest Group and Walton Street Capital purchased the Mercy Medical Commons campus in Gilbert, Arizona, comprising two fully leased medical office buildings totaling 105,715 SF on 11 acres. The 2010-built first building (47,017 SF) and 2020-built second building (58,698 SF) are occupied by nine healthcare providers, positioned across from Mercy Gilbert Medical Center's 400-bed campus. The transaction reflects strong healthcare real estate demand in the rapidly growing Southeast Valley.
stories.impact: Gilbert's population and employment growth are driving healthcare and office demand, creating a secondary effect: rising demand for multifamily housing to support in-migrating workers. Developers should acquire/entitle multifamily near medical office clusters in Gilbert and broader Southeast Phoenix, as healthcare employment anchors long-term population retention and rent growth.

stories.title: Convenience Store and Fuel Station in Colorado Traded for $5.35M
stories.excerpt: A 4,973-square-foot Maverik convenience store and fuel station in Colorado Springs, Colorado, was sold in a $5.35 million transaction. The property sits on 2.02 acres at 6735 Carefree Circle, at the signalized intersection of Peterson Road and Carefree Circle North. The site includes 20 fuel pumps and benefits from visibility along a corridor with more than 9,600 vehicles per day. It is adjacent to Sand Creek High School and near national retailers including Target, TJ Maxx, HomeGoods, JCPenney, Best Buy and Lowe’s. The property is occupied by Maverik under an absolute triple-net lease, with no landlord responsibilities. The location has operated since 2013, first as a Kum & Go and later under the Maverik brand. The lease includes four five-year renewal options. Matt Nora, Kirk Vanino and Jack D’Avanzo with Lee & Associates, Denver represented the seller, Hanlon Bush Investments LLC. The post Convenience Store and Fuel Station in Colorado Traded for $5.35M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Maverik convenience store and fuel station sold in Colorado Springs for $5.35M; 2.02 acres.
Site sits at Peterson Road and Carefree Circle North; 9,600 vehicles/day; triple-net lease.
Adjacent to Sand Creek High School and retail anchors (Target, Best Buy, Lowe's).
stories.summary: A 4,973 SF Maverik convenience and fuel station at 6735 Carefree Circle in Colorado Springs sold for $5.35 million. The 2.02-acre site features 20 fuel pumps, 9,600 daily vehicles, and sits in a retail-anchored node near Sand Creek High School. The property operates under an absolute triple-net lease with four five-year renewal options, occupied by Maverik since 2013.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. However, the site's location in a high-traffic retail corridor signals density and retail consolidation in this Colorado Springs submarket; developers should monitor whether such nodes eventually densify with transit or mixed-use, creating long-term multifamily upside.

stories.title: Mary Kay Moving into 12-Story Plano Tower
stories.excerpt: Cosmetics giant Mary Kay sold its 546,000-square-foot headquarters campus in Addison and is moving its headquarters to six floors of Legacy Union One, a 12-story tower in The Shops at Legacy East in Plano. Mary Kay will occupy nearly 160,000 square feet across six floors, becoming its primary tenant. The interior will be designed by Corgan. The new headquarters is bringing corporate employees closer to the company’s Richard R. Rogers Manufacturing/R&D Center in Lewisville. Known as R3, the global facility opened in 2018 following an investment of more than $100 million. The 453,000-square-foot center houses research, development and manufacturing operations, with the capacity to produce up to 1 million units of product each day across 22 packaging lines. Its output supports Mary Kay’s business in 40 markets worldwide. The company’s regional footprint also includes logistics facilities, making the move to Plano part of a broader North Texas presence rather than a departure from its existing operations. The post Mary Kay Moving into 12-Story Plano Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Mary Kay relocates HQ from Addison to Plano; moves 160,000 SF into 6 floors of Legacy Union One.
Sold 546,000 SF Addison campus; consolidating operations near R3 manufacturing center in Lewisville.
Headquarters move reflects North Texas logistics/manufacturing footprint optimization.
stories.summary: Mary Kay sold its 546,000 SF headquarters campus in Addison and is relocating to six floors (nearly 160,000 SF) of the 12-story Legacy Union One tower in Plano's Shops at Legacy East. The move positions corporate staff closer to its $100M+ R3 manufacturing and R&D facility in Lewisville, which opened in 2018 and produces 1 million units daily for 40 global markets. The relocation is part of a broader North Texas footprint consolidation, not an exit.
stories.impact: Major corporate headquarters relocation from Addison to Plano signals potential multifamily demand shift within Dallas; Plano will see increased white-collar employment density and in-migration, supporting rent growth in Legacy/Park Cities submarkets. Addison loses a large anchor employer, potentially softening demand; developers should build/acquire in Plano's proximity to Legacy Union One and monitor Addison for value-add opportunities or selective repositioning.

stories.title: Merchants Capital Secures $15M for Affordable Housing Development
stories.excerpt: Indiana-based Merchants Capital announced $15.5 million in financing for the construction of Ryans Way, a 60-unit low-income housing tax credit (LIHTC) development in Charlotte, North Carolina, developed by Scantland, Inc.Merchants Capital secured $11.1 million in federal LIHTC as the syndicator for Ryans Way. It also arranged $4.4 million in Freddie Mac Forward permanent financing to facilitate construction loan refinancing. “Merchants Capital’s ability to align debt and equity sources across the capital stack enables us to provide efficient, tailored financing solutions for our partners,” said Marcin Dzido, Vice President of Acquisitions at Merchants Capital.Ryans Way includes two three-story, garden-style residential buildings with one-, two-, and three-bedroom units and a multi-purpose community building. The development will be located in close proximity to retail, recreation areas, parks, medical facilities and schools. Construction began in October 2026 and is expected to be completed in 18 months. Join us for the Connect Midwest Multifamily conference on the afternoon of Tuesday, June 8, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont, Illinois. The post Merchants Capital Secures $15M for Affordable Housing Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Merchants Capital secures $15.5M for Ryans Way, 60-unit LIHTC development in Charlotte, NC.
Financing includes $11.1M federal LIHTC and $4.4M Freddie Mac Forward permanent financing.
Low-income housing development demonstrates continued affordable housing capital availability.
stories.summary: Merchants Capital announced $15.5 million in financing for Ryans Way, a 60-unit low-income housing tax credit (LIHTC) development in Charlotte, North Carolina, developed by Scantland, Inc. Merchants Capital syndicated $11.1 million in federal LIHTC and arranged $4.4 million in Freddie Mac Forward permanent financing to refinance construction debt. The capital stack demonstrates alignment of debt and equity sources for affordable housing.
stories.impact: LIHTC and permanent financing availability remain strong for affordable multifamily in Charlotte; signals sustained appetite from Freddie Mac and tax credit syndicators. Developers should note Charlotte's affordable housing tailwind and position projects accordingly; this also indicates regulatory/political support for affordable housing, reducing entitlement risk in the market.

stories.title: Colliers Completes Lease at Indiana Industrial Development, Bringing Property to Full Occupancy
stories.excerpt: Colliers represented CPUS Anson Building 8A, LP, the landlord entity for CBRE Investment Management, in a new 184,140-square-foot lease at Anson 8A, located at 4255 South 500 East in Whitestown, Indiana. The transaction brings Anson 8A to 100% leased, completing the building’s lease-up. The lease was led by the Colliers | Indianapolis team of Jason Speckman, SIOR, and Jimmy Cohoat, SIOR. Zachary Binswanger of Binswanger International represented Hessaire Products, Inc., a manufacturer of cooling solutions. “This transaction represents a significant milestone for ownership and highlights the sustained demand for well-located, high-quality industrial facilities in Central Indiana,” said Speckman. “We are pleased to welcome Hessaire Products to Anson 8A and deliver a successful leasing outcome for our client.” Completed in 2017, Anson 8A is a modern industrial facility designed to accommodate a wide range of logistics and distribution users. Located in one of Central Indiana’s most active industrial and logistics corridors, the facility provides strategic access to the Indianapolis metropolitan area. Mark Goode to Receive Lifetime Achievement Award at Connect Industrial Midwest on Tuesday, March 2, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont. Following the presentation, Mark Goode will sit down for a special keynote interview with his son, Matt Goode. bullets: Colliers completes 184,140 SF lease at Anson 8A, Whitestown, Indiana; building now 100% leased.
Hessaire Products (cooling solutions manufacturer) signed the lease; Anson 8A completed 2017.
Central Indiana industrial corridor demonstrates sustained demand for logistics and distribution facilities.
stories.summary: Colliers represented ownership (CPUS Anson Building 8A, LP) in leasing 184,140 SF to Hessaire Products, Inc., a cooling solutions manufacturer, bringing the Anson 8A industrial facility in Whitestown, Indiana to full occupancy. Completed in 2017, the building is a modern logistics and distribution facility in one of Central Indiana's most active industrial corridors. The lease-up milestone reflects sustained demand for well-located, high-quality industrial space.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance; however, strong industrial absorption in Central Indiana's logistics corridor signals job growth and in-migration, supporting residential demand in Indianapolis and Whitestown submarkets. Multifamily developers should acquire sites near Anson Industrial Park and other logistics nodes to capture workforce housing demand from manufacturing and warehousing employers.

stories.title: Law Firm MoloLamken Relocates to 25K SF at RXR’s 590 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: Law firm MoloLamken is relocating its Midtown Manhattan offices to RXR’s 590 Madison Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. The boutique law firm, which specializes in complex litigation, struck a deal for 24,839 square feet across the entire 16th floor of the office tower, according to an RXR spokesperson. MoloLamken’s moving day should be a breeze – the firm’s new space sits just one block west of its current office at 430 Park Avenue. The firm’s new lease carries a 10-year term. Its precise rent was not disclosed, but asking rents throughout the building range from $155 to $205 per square foot, according to RXR. Savills’ Joe Learner and Jarod Stern negotiated the deal on behalf of MoloLamken, while RXR was represented in-house by Daniel Birney and Heidi Steinegger. “With a global client base, the firm further positions the building as a hub for international talent across law, finance and fashion,” RXR’s William Elder said in a statement. MoloLamken’s arrival comes after a particularly busy year for 590 Madison. The 43-story tower at the corner of Madison Avenue and East 57th Street traded to RXR with a whopping $1.08 billion price tag last summer, marking the city’s first billion-dollar sale since 2018. The 1 million-square-foot office tower, once known as the IBM Building, has undergone a substantial overhaul since RXR took over. Recent additions include a new 25,000-square-foot amenity center and a 2,800-square-foot terrace. MoloLamken’s new home on the tower’s 16th floor sits just above another new arrival. A platform company under the Apollo Global Management umbrella secured the tower’s 14th and 15th floors in April, CO previously reported, one year after Apollo inked its own three-story spread across the building’s 10th, 12th and 13th floors. Other corporate tenants in the building include financial firm Mak Capital and financial consultancy Odyssey Investment Partners. Spokespeople for MoloLamken and Savills did not reply to requests for comment. Emily
bullets: MoloLamken law firm leases 24,839 SF (entire 16th floor) at RXR's 590 Madison Avenue, Manhattan.
10-year lease; asking rents range $155–$205/SF; firm relocates from 430 Park Avenue (1 block west).
Boutique litigation firm signals office demand in Midtown Manhattan office towers.
stories.summary: MoloLamken, a boutique complex litigation law firm, signed a 10-year lease for 24,839 SF—the entire 16th floor of RXR's 590 Madison Avenue in Midtown Manhattan. The firm is relocating from 430 Park Avenue, one block west, with asking rents at the building ranging $155–$205/SF. The transaction underscores continued office demand among high-caliber professional services tenants seeking prestige locations.
stories.impact: Office leasing activity at trophy Midtown Manhattan buildings signals stabilization and tenant demand in core markets post-hybrid; however, this benefits RXR's office portfolio, not multifamily. No meaningful secondary effect on residential demand; Midtown's multifamily is driven by population/job growth, not office occupancy churn.

stories.title: Loudoun County, U.S. Data Center Capital, Pauses New Data Center Projects
stories.excerpt: Infographic with a satellite image showing new buildings constructed between 2002 and 2025 in Ashburn, Va. known for the density of its data centers. GRAPHIC: Sophie RAMIS and Yann SCHREIBER / AFP via Getty Images Loudoun County, Va., home to the world’s largest concentration of data centers, has approved a 12-month pause on entitling new data centers and electrical substations while officials craft tighter restrictions on the rapidly expanding asset class. The county’s Board of Supervisors voted 7-1 Tuesday evening to halt consideration of applications for the facilities that require special zoning exceptions. One supervisor abstained. The pause is retroactive to Sept. 15, when the board first directed staff to prepare the resolution. Developers can still submit applications, but supervisors will delay consideration for up to 12 months from when the applications reach the Planning Commission. During the moratorium, Loudoun officials plan to update land use standards for digital infrastructure, including where the facilities can be developed. Loudoun has 33 active applications involving data centers and substations. Separately, according to media reports, 15 to 17 grandfathered data center projects or administrative applications under earlier zoning rules can advance despite the pause. (New substations needed for grid reliability and certain zoning conversions in the Route 28 corridor are exempt from the pause.) The county could face a lengthy backlog when approvals resume. County staff estimates that clearing delayed applications could require four to six months of additional meetings beginning in fall 2027. The measure also faces potential legal challenges. Data center developers argued that delaying approvals would undermine investor confidence and disrupt projects planned under existing regulations. The vote represents another significant reversal for a county that spent decades encouraging data center construction. Commercial Observer previously reported Loudou
bullets: Loudoun County, Virginia pauses new data center entitlements for 12 months; moratorium retroactive to Sept. 15.
Board voted 7-1 to halt special zoning exceptions; 33 active applications deferred up to 12 months.
County plans tighter digital infrastructure land-use standards during pause.
stories.summary: Loudoun County, Virginia's Board of Supervisors voted 7-1 to impose a 12-month moratorium on new data center and electrical substation entitlements, effective retroactively from September 15. Developers may still submit applications, but the Planning Commission will delay consideration for up to 12 months. During the pause, Loudoun officials will update land-use standards for digital infrastructure, restricting where facilities can be developed.
stories.impact: Data center moratorium in Loudoun reduces industrial/land demand and construction activity in the region, reducing short-term labor demand but removing an inflationary industrial cost pressure. For multifamily: slower data center job in-migration near Ashburn and Leesburg may dampen near-term wage and population growth, cooling rent appreciation in Northern Virginia. Developers should monitor when the moratorium lifts (Q4 2025–Q1 2026) for potential re-acceleration.

stories.title: Aaru Signs 27K-SF Sublease in Union Square With Plans for 650 NYC Employees
stories.excerpt: A rapidly expanding artificial intelligence platform known for having “rage rooms” in its offices and other perks has signed a new lease near Manhattan’s Union Square. Aaru, founded only about two years ago, has signed a deal for 27,238 square feet to facilitate a five-year expansion plan from a headcount of 60 to about 650 employees in New York City at ZG Capital Partners’ 836–838 Broadway, according to an announcement from Gov. Kathy Hochul. Aaru currently has offices at 199 Lafayette Street in Tribeca. The deal is a sublease with artificial intelligence platform Legora, which leased the space through 2031. “We made a deliberate decision to build Aaru in New York City,” Aaru co-founder and CEO Cameron Fink said in a statement. “The depth and diversity of talent here, proximity to the world’s largest enterprises, and the city’s history of innovation make it the right place for what we’re building. Being a New York company is core to our DNA.” Lenny Kohlmayer and Evan Kleinberg of Cornelia Street Partners represented Aaru alongside Zachary Weil, Brent Ozarowski and Cole Gendels of Newmark, while Justin Haber, Kyle Riker and Emma Gill of JLL negotiated on behalf of Legora. bullets: Aaru AI platform signs 27,238 SF sublease in Union Square, Manhattan; expands from 60 to 650 NYC employees.
Five-year expansion plan at 836–838 Broadway; sublease through Legora; currently at 199 Lafayette, Tribeca.
Rapidly expanding AI startup signals sustained office demand and tech in-migration to Manhattan.
stories.summary: Aaru, a two-year-old artificial intelligence platform, signed a 27,238 SF sublease at 836–838 Broadway in Union Square as part of a five-year expansion plan to grow from 60 to 650 employees in New York City. The deal is a sublease through Legora, an AI platform, running through 2031. Aaru currently occupies space at 199 Lafayette in Tribeca and cited NYC's talent depth, enterprise proximity, and innovation history as key to its expansion decision.
stories.impact: High-growth AI/tech hiring in Manhattan signals sustained professional job creation and in-migration, supporting multifamily demand across Manhattan and outer-borough submarkets. Developers should monitor AI sector cluster formation (Union Square, Tribeca, broader Manhattan tech hubs) and prioritize acquisition/development near these employment nodes for luxury and upper-mid multifamily—tech talent attracts premium rents and long lease terms.
